analysis:
All three changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/...); no production source, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, or cache storage code is modified, so no runtime security regression is introduced by this diff.

1) GLM5ToolFailureTests.swift (L33-50): the test that asserted forced tool_choice was refused for GLM is replaced by one asserting forced choice is served via the native GLM parser, which withholds calls until EOS (structuredPostValidation). The tests at L52-93 assert that a malformed or truncated suffix emits no tool call and no visible content (no plaintext leak, T-008 spirit) and that the failure maps to 422 or 500. This documents a production behavior change (forced GLM tool choice now allowed) whose implementation is outside the supplied evidence. The production handler and ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy should be reviewed when that source is in a batch.

2) GLM5NextMediaRoutingTests.swift: adds a test that JSON response_format and required/named tool_choice with image or video input are refused before any media preparation (capture.requests and engine.submitted both empty). This is a fail-closed control. It adds video tests using OpenRouter fixtures pinned by SHA-256 and a marker tokenizer. The fixture path comes from #filePath, which is a test-only concern. The media ingest/processor code (T-050-style temp-file exposure, resource budgets) is not in the diff.

3) GLM5NextProviderLoopTests.swift: adds a test that the load publishes its verified digest with no WeightHasher bracketing reads, that the live hash equals the manifest aggregate, and that the VerifiedWeightHashStore record matches. This relates to T-012/T-027 (weight substitution). The production change implying that the load-time SHA-256 check replaces separate hashing is not in the supplied files. The next pass should confirm that the load-time verification actually covers every weight file read, and that VerifiedWeightHashStore's file-identity (size/mtime) record cannot be used to skip re-verification after an operator swaps weights while preserving the identity.

No ADV/threat-model assumption is invalidated by the supplied test code.
